text: The sky appears blue because molecules in the Earth's atmosphere scatter shorter blue wavelengths of light more than longer red wavelengths, a phenomenon known as Rayleigh scattering. As sunlight passes through the atmosphere, this scattering causes the blue light to be dispersed in all directions, making the sky look blue to our eyes. What is the main reason the sky appears blue? The main reason the sky appears blue is due to Rayleigh scattering, where molecules in the atmosphere scatter shorter blue wavelengths of sunlight more than other colors.
